name: Case A - Inspect the mock bay
brief: A classroom wall mockup must be checked against Issued Drawing A. Use the supplied survey below, or a teacher-verified physical mockup with its own survey. These numbers are simulated teaching data, not a survey of the fieldhouse. The lower-left outside corner is the datum. All dimensions are inches. Length/position specifications have +/-1/8 inch tolerance. The pipe OD note must match the supplied material reference.
deliverables: Write the purpose, constraints, evidence source and information still missing before a real job.
Complete an inspection table: feature, spec/interval, reading, signed deviation, in/out and amount outside.
Produce an as-built elevation with corrected positions/dimensions and service note. Add an appropriate section or orthographic view to clarify one interface.
Write a short inspection note identifying what changes and why. Distinguish a material-label error from a tolerance failure.
key: Width: +1/16, in. Height: 0, in. Opening width: -1/4 from target, below lower limit by 1/8, out. Opening left edge: +1/4 from target, above upper limit by 1/8, out. Service center: +1/16, in. Service OD note: replace 2 with 2 3/8 inches; nominal size is not OD. A revision should preserve the survey, not change it to the intended dimensions. Do not infer opening height or service fitting dimensions: they were not supplied and must be flagged.
exemplar: The opening is 15 3/4 in wide. The allowed interval is 15 7/8 to 16 1/8, so it is 1/8 below the lower limit. Its left edge is also 1/8 beyond its upper positional limit. I recorded both on revision B and corrected the service OD note to 2 3/8 in. The source is provided classroom survey data; before using this as a field drawing I need an instrument-checked survey, missing opening height, service fittings and approved details.
partial: The opening is too small because 15 3/4 is less than 16. Fix it. This identifies a discrepancy but omits the tolerance interval, amount outside, position error, evidence source and correction detail.
new_evidence: Repeat one personally measured feature with a checked reference, or correct the supplied-data interval calculation; submit a revised drawing and explain exactly how the new evidence changed the decision.

name: Case B - Route the drain through the service zone
brief: This is a dry classroom coordination model, not an installation approval or permission to alter framing. Original horizontal run is 18 ft; available service-zone depth is 8 in. Required slope is at least 1/4 in/ft. Pipe OD is 2 3/8 in. Minimum top and bottom clearances are 3/4 in each. All vertical dimensions use the zone top as datum. Two changes may be proposed for review: shorten the run to 16 ft, or deepen the zone to 8 1/2 in while keeping the 18-ft run. Other fittings, access and connections are not specified.
deliverables: List fixed requirements and the two changes available for review.
Calculate original fall, required depth and quantified conflict. Reject an unsupported slope reduction.
Evaluate both alternatives, including remaining depth margin.
Draw a plan and longitudinal section for your proposed route: flow, horizontal run, slope, datum, elevations and outside envelope.
Write an RFI explaining what another trade must confirm before the proposal could be used.
key: Original fall 18 x 1/4 = 4 1/2 in. Required depth 3/4 + 2 3/8 + 4 1/2 + 3/4 = 8 3/8 in. Shortfall 3/8 in. Alternative 1: fall 4 in; total 7 7/8; margin 1/8 in. Alternative 2: original required 8 3/8 in inside 8 1/2; margin 1/8 in. With zone top datum and upstream pipe outer top 3/4 in down, center starts 1 15/16 in down. Original downstream center is 6 7/16 down; 16-ft alternative center is 5 15/16 down. Original downstream outer bottom is 7 5/8 down. Both alternatives are geometric proposals only: neither accounts for unspecified fittings or authorizes structural changes.
exemplar: The original route needs 8 3/8 inches but only 8 is available, so it fails by 3/8 inch. I propose the 16-foot route: fall is 4 inches, total envelope including clearances is 7 7/8 inches, leaving 1/8 inch. My plan and section retain 1/4 in/ft and show the common top datum. The shorter route must be checked for connections, fittings and access; the carpenter/plumber must confirm the coordinated detail before work.
partial: It fits because the fall is only 4 1/2 inches and the bay is 8. This omits OD and both clearances, so the central feasibility claim is incorrect even though the fall calculation is right.
new_evidence: Correct the complete depth budget, add missing dimensions to both views, and test the selected route against the stated constraints. Submit a revision note showing which previous claim changed.
